# #1776: Patch: a Buffed spell's Pierce is proven to go through Armor, and the damage steps say a spell's keywords come through Buffs
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means
Since the latest Buff change, a Buff can give a damage spell Pierce (its damage ignores Armor) or Lifesteal, and a Field Spell Indestructible. The game already plays all three right, but only Lifesteal has a test for the spell case, and the rules text a builder reads still says a spell pierces only when Pierce is printed on it. A later change that followed that text would quietly break Buffed spells, and nothing would fail. Once built, a test pins the Pierce half, and the rules text matches the game.

## Why
- R1748001 (#1748, shipped in #1752) says a Buffed "Pierce one pierces, as a printed keyword does". Its spell test, `r1748001_a_damage_spell_may_gain_pierce_or_lifesteal_and_its_lifesteal_heals` (`crates/cards/tests/cross/buff_priorities.rs:136`), checks only the Lifesteal heal. Nothing casts a Buffed Pierce spell at a hero or unit with Armor.
- §4.4 step 2 (`spec/04-combat.md:52`) still reads "a unit's Pierce through the layers, a spell's printed on its face (True Strike, [[R346]])", and §6.1's Pierce row (`spec/06-keywords.md:28`) says the same. #1752 edited only the Nerf row of `06-keywords.md` and left `04-combat.md` untouched.
- The engine reads the layers for every source (`crates/engine/src/damage.rs:368-378`, `pierces` → `layers::unit_view(state, source).keywords`), so it plays right today, but narrowing it to printed keywords, as the text says, would break no test.
- §4.5 step 1 speaks of Indestructible units only, though a Buff can now make a Field Spell Indestructible (`crates/engine/src/state_check.rs` handles it, and R1748001's first test proves it).

## Proposal
- Add an `r1748001_…` test: Lunar Eclipse (`core-035`) given Pierce through its `tuning`, cast at a hero with Armor, deals its full damage and is no `damageAbsorbed`. Add a second case for a damage-dealing Field Spell such as The Power to Punish (`classic-020`) given Pierce.
- Fix the text of §4.4 step 2 and §6.1's Pierce row ("a spell's through its Buffs as well as its face", citing [[R1748001]]), §4.5 step 1 for an Indestructible Field Spell, and §6.1's Lifesteal and Indestructible rows if they say "printed".
- R1748001 already decides all of this, so no new ruling is needed. List the test's file in its `proven_in` if it is a new file, and run `cargo jackioh spec index` and `spec check`.

## Where it lands
- `crates/cards/tests/cross/buff_priorities.rs`
- `spec/04-combat.md` (§4.4, §4.5), `spec/06-keywords.md` (§6.1), `spec/INDEX.md`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The new test fails when `pierces` is narrowed to a source's printed keywords, and passes at HEAD.
- [ ] §4.4 step 2 and §6.1's Pierce row say a spell's Pierce may come from a Buff, citing R1748001.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-cards --test cards buff_priorities` and `cargo jackioh spec check` pass.
- [ ] No card plays differently: the classifier finds no change, so no fragment is needed.

## Size and risks
Small: one test file and three spec paragraphs. Medium (spec text). No risk to play.

## Plan

_Written by `claude-8` (claude, `opus`, strong) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/40073288405)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

Add a test proving that a Buff's Pierce on a damage-dealing spell goes through Armor, and make the rules text say so. R1748001 already decides this.

Done means:
- `crates/cards/tests/cross/buff_priorities.rs` has two new `r1748001_…` tests:
  - Lunar Eclipse (`core-035`) is given Pierce through its `tuning` and hits a hero with Armor.
  - The Power to Punish (`classic-020`) is given Pierce the same way and hits a Unit with Armor.
- Both tests pass at HEAD and fail when `pierces` reads only printed keywords.
- §4.4 step 2 and §6.1's Pierce row say a spell's Pierce may come from a Buff, citing [[R1748001]].
- §4.5 step 1 covers an Indestructible Field Spell.
- No ruling note, catalog entry, card or fragment changes.

## Files to touch

| File | new/change | What |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `crates/cards/tests/cross/buff_priorities.rs` | change | 3 consts (`PUNISH`, `PUNISH_DAMAGE`, `ARMORED`), 3 helpers (`give_pierce`, `count`, `hits`), 2 tests |
| `spec/04-combat.md` | change | §4.4 step 2: one sentence reworded. §4.5 step 1: one sentence added |
| `spec/06-keywords.md` | change | §6.1 table, `Pierce` row, Engine semantics cell: one clause reworded |
| `crates/engine/src/damage.rs` | change | Only the doc comment above `pub fn pierces` (lines 368–373). No code |

**Do not touch:**
- `spec/INDEX.md`: `cargo jackioh spec index` must leave it unchanged.
- Any `spec/rulings/*.md`, including `R0346.md` and `R1748001.md`.
- `spec/11-rulings.md`.
- `crates/cards/catalog.json` and `crates/cards/patches/`.
- Any card script.
- Any engine code other than that comment.
- `apps/web`.

**Governing:**
- SPEC §4.4 step 2, step 5 and the zero rule (`damageAbsorbed`).
- §4.5 step 1.
- §6.1 Pierce and Indestructible.
- §6.3 Nerf and Buff.
- Rulings R346, R1360, R1361, R46 and R1748001.

## Steps

1. **`crates/cards/tests/cross/buff_priorities.rs`: constants.** Insert these right after the line `const FIELD_OF_DREAMS: &str = "core-076"; // (2) Spell that deals no damage.` and before `const FILLER`:
   ```rust
   const PUNISH: &str = "classic-020"; // The Power to Punish: (2) Field Spell, Activate deals 2, `dealsDamage`.
   const PUNISH_DAMAGE: &str = "deal damage"; // Its Activate's damage mode.
   const ARMORED: &str = "core-025"; // A 7/7 Unit with Armor 7.
   ```

2. **Same file: helpers.** Insert these right after `fn has(…) { … }` and before the first `#[test]`:
   ```rust
   /// Pierce given to the card `card` names, as a Buff's keyword row leaves it (`tuning`).
   fn give_pierce(s: &mut Scenario, card: &str) {
       s.card_mut(card).tuning = Some(Tuning {
           add_keywords: Some(vec![Keyword::Pierce]),
           ..Tuning::default()
       });
   }

   /// How many events of that type the scenario has seen since setup.
   fn count(s: &Scenario, event_type: GameEventType) -> usize {
       s.events()
           .iter()
           .filter(|event| event.event_type() == event_type)
           .count()
   }

   /// Each `damage` event's amount dealt and the part of the hit its target's Armor took (`absorbed`, R1360).
   fn hits(s: &Scenario) -> Vec<(i32, i32)> {
       s.events()
           .iter()
           .filter_map(|event| match event {
               GameEvent::Damage { amount, absorbed, .. } => Some((*amount, *absorbed)),
               _ => None,
           })
           .collect()
   }
   ```
   No new `use` is needed: `jackioh_engine::testkit::*` already brings `Tuning`, `Keyword`, `GameEvent`, `GameEventType` and `json!`.

3. **Same file: two tests.** Insert them right after `r1748001_a_damage_spell_may_gain_pierce_or_lifesteal_and_its_lifesteal_heals` and before `#[test] fn r1748002_…`:
   ```rust
   #[test]
   fn r1748001_a_spell_a_buff_gives_pierce_goes_through_a_heros_armor() {
       let eclipse_at_p2 = |pierce: bool| {
           let mut s = scenario(json!({
               "p1": { "hand": [ECLIPSE, FILLER] },
               "p2": { "hand": [FILLER], "armor": 3 },
           }));
           if pierce {
               give_pierce(&mut s, ECLIPSE);
           }
           s.play(
               ECLIPSE,
               json!({ "targets": [{ "pick": "hero", "player": "p2" }] }),
           );
           s
       };

       // Unbuffed, p2's Armor 3 takes the whole of its 3 damage.
       let mut s = eclipse_at_p2(false);
       s.expect_health(P2, 30);
       assert!(hits(&s).is_empty());
       assert_eq!(count(&s, GameEventType::DamageAbsorbed), 1);

       // Given Pierce, all 3 land and the Armor takes nothing.
       let mut s = eclipse_at_p2(true);
       s.expect_health(P2, 27);
       assert_eq!(hits(&s), [(3, 0)]);
       assert_eq!(count(&s, GameEventType::DamageAbsorbed), 0);
   }

   #[test]
   fn r1748001_a_field_spell_a_buff_gives_pierce_goes_through_a_units_armor() {
       let punish_at_armored = |pierce: bool| {
           let mut s = scenario(json!({
               "p1": { "hand": [FILLER], "backrow": [{ "def": PUNISH, "faceUp": true }] },
               "p2": { "hand": [FILLER], "field": [ARMORED] },
           }));
           if pierce {
               give_pierce(&mut s, PUNISH);
           }
           let target = s.card(ARMORED).id.clone();
           s.activate(
               PUNISH,
               json!({
                   "modes": [PUNISH_DAMAGE],
                   "targets": [{ "pick": "instance", "instanceId": target }],
               }),
           );
           s
       };

       // Unbuffed, the Unit's Armor 7 takes the whole of its 2 damage.
       let s = punish_at_armored(false);
       assert_eq!(s.stats(ARMORED).health, 7);
       assert!(hits(&s).is_empty());
       assert_eq!(count(&s, GameEventType::DamageAbsorbed), 1);

       // Given Pierce, both land and the Armor takes nothing.
       let s = punish_at_armored(true);
       assert_eq!(s.stats(ARMORED).health, 5);
       assert_eq!(hits(&s), [(2, 0)]);
       assert_eq!(count(&s, GameEventType::DamageAbsorbed), 0);
   }
   ```
   Leave the module doc comment (lines 1–5) unchanged: it already names R1748001's Pierce.

4. **`spec/04-combat.md`, §4.4 step 2 (line 52).** Replace exactly
   `A source with Pierce skips this, on a unit and on a hero alike: a unit's Pierce through the layers, a spell's printed on its face (True Strike, [[R346]]).`
   with
   `A source with Pierce skips this, on a unit and on a hero alike: a unit's Pierce through the layers, and a Spell's or a Field Spell's the same way, whether printed on its face (True Strike, [[R346]]) or given by a Buff ([[R1748001]]).`
   Leave the rest of the step as it is.

5. **`spec/04-combat.md`, §4.5 step 1 (line 66).** Right after the sentence ending `…loses Taunt until end of turn ([[R46]]).` insert one space and then:
   `An Indestructible Field Spell, printed (#98 Heroic Power) or given it by a Buff ([[R1748001]]), ignores its destroy mark too and keeps its backrow zone; it has no position or Taunt to lose.`
   This matches `resolve_indestructible_marks` in `crates/engine/src/state_check.rs`, which drops the mark of an Indestructible backrow card.

6. **`spec/06-keywords.md`, §6.1 table, `| Pierce |` row (line 28), Engine semantics cell.** Replace exactly
   `a unit's keyword read through the layers, or a spell's printed on its face ([[R346]])`
   with
   `a unit's keyword read through the layers, and a Spell's or a Field Spell's the same way, whether printed on its face ([[R346]]) or given by a Buff ([[R1748001]])`
   Leave the first column and the Cards column unchanged. `apps/web/src/cards/rules.test.ts` reads the first column.

7. **`crates/engine/src/damage.rs`, doc comment of `pub fn pierces`.** Replace lines 369–373 (from `/// the layers like its Lifesteal…` through `/// cap and Indestructible all still apply.`) with:
   ```rust
   /// the layers like its Lifesteal and Trample (§10.4), or a spell's, printed on its face (#44 True
   /// Strike) or given by a Buff (R1748001), which the same reading finds on the card while it resolves —
   /// or the effect's own `ignore_armor`, which states that its damage pierces without the source having
   /// the keyword, as R85's `lifesteal` does for Lifesteal. It skips step 2 and nothing else: Divine
   /// Shield, the hero cap and Indestructible all still apply.
   ```
   Line 368 (`/// R346: whether a hit skips…`) and the function body stay as they are.

8. **Mutation check, then revert.**
   - In `pierces`, temporarily change `&crate::layers::unit_view(state, source).keywords,` to `&crate::layers::printed_keywords_of(state, source),`.
   - Run `cargo test -p jackioh-cards --test cards buff_priorities`. Both new tests must FAIL and the four old ones must pass.
   - Restore the line by hand and confirm `git diff crates/engine/src/damage.rs` shows only step 7's comment.

9. **Rulings index.** Run `cargo jackioh spec index`, then confirm `git status --porcelain spec/INDEX.md` prints nothing. No note's title or `proven_in` changed, and `buff_priorities.rs` is already in R1748001's `proven_in`.

## Tests

File: `crates/cards/tests/cross/buff_priorities.rs`.

`r1748001_a_spell_a_buff_gives_pierce_goes_through_a_heros_armor` asserts:
- **Unbuffed:** Lunar Eclipse at p2 (Armor 3) leaves p2 at 30, with no `damage` event and one `damageAbsorbed`.
- **Given Pierce:** p2 is at 27, with one `damage` of 3 and `absorbed` 0, and no `damageAbsorbed`.

`r1748001_a_field_spell_a_buff_gives_pierce_goes_through_a_units_armor` asserts:
- **Unbuffed:** The Power to Punish's "deal damage" mode at core-025 (Armor 7) leaves it at 7 health, with one `damageAbsorbed`.
- **Given Pierce:** it is at 5, with one `damage` of 2 and `absorbed` 0, and no `damageAbsorbed`.

A planner's trial run on a scratch copy of HEAD showed:
- 6/6 `buff_priorities` tests pass.
- Under step 8's mutation, both new tests fail.
- `cargo fmt --check` is clean.
- `cargo clippy -p jackioh-cards --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.
- `spec index` makes no diff.
- `spec check` is ok.

Commands:
```
cargo test -p jackioh-cards --test cards buff_priorities
cargo fmt --check
cargo clippy -p jackioh-cards --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo clippy -p jackioh-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo jackioh spec index && git status --porcelain spec/INDEX.md
cargo jackioh spec check
cargo jackioh classify --base origin/main --claims
sh scripts/build-wasm.sh && pnpm --dir apps/web exec vitest run src/cards/rules.test.ts
```
- `classify` must find no card that plays differently, so no fragment is needed.
- The last command is the web test that parses `06-keywords.md`. It needs the wasm build first.

## Done when

- [ ] Both new tests pass, and step 8 showed both failing under the printed-keywords mutation, with the engine code restored.
- [ ] §4.4 step 2 and §6.1's Pierce row say a spell's Pierce may come from a Buff, citing [[R1748001]].
- [ ] §4.5 step 1 covers an Indestructible Field Spell.
- [ ] `damage.rs` differs from HEAD only in the `pierces` doc comment.
- [ ] `spec/INDEX.md` is unchanged, and no file under `spec/rulings/` is changed.
- [ ] rustfmt, clippy, `spec check`, `catalog check`, `patches check` and the cargo tests are green.
- [ ] `classify --claims` finds no card change, and no fragment is added.
- [ ] `rules.test.ts` passes.
- [ ] The PR body records the decisions below.

## Risks

- **Play, determinism, replay, hidden information:** none. Only a test, prose and a comment change.
- **Leaving the step 8 mutation in place** would change play. Revert it and check `git diff`.
- **`spec check` rule 6 (INDEX):** editing a ruling note's `title` or `proven_in` would change the index. Edit no note.
- **`rules.test.ts` reads the first cell of every §6.1 row.** Do not edit the `Pierce` name cell, and do not add a `|` inside the cell.
- **Line width:** keep every new Rust line at or under `max_width = 110`. The `PUNISH` comment above is already shortened to fit.

## Decisions (record in the PR)

1. The tests set `tuning` directly instead of driving a seeded `upgrade`.
   - Why: R1748001's Lifesteal test already does it this way, and `r1748001_a_damage_spell_may_gain_pierce_or_lifesteal…` already proves the row draw.
   - Rejected: a `seed_where` search for a seed whose Buff draws Pierce.
2. The Field Spell case aims at a Unit with Armor, so the pair covers both targets §4.4 step 2 names.
   - Rejected: a second hero case.
3. §6.1's Lifesteal and Indestructible rows say nothing of "printed", so they are left as they are. The issue asked for those rows only if they do.
4. §4.4 step 9's Trample clause ("read off its face as a spell's Pierce is") is left as it is.
   - Why: a Buff never gives Trample (`TUNE_DAMAGE_KEYWORDS` holds only Pierce and Lifesteal), and the reading is the same one.
5. `R0346.md`'s body and `spec/11-rulings.md`'s R1748000–R1748003 summary are left as they are. A ruling records its decision, and R1748001 is the later one.
6. The `pierces` doc comment is updated because it repeats the "printed on its face" wording that could mislead the same way.
   - Rejected: leaving it out of scope.

## Open questions

None.
